sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, Arran
sources.note: 1986 scholarly regional entry. Medieval Kura-Aras usage is narrower than ancient Caucasian Albania. Its attribution of the 1075 conquest to Alp Arslan conflicts with his death; use Peacock for that event.

sources.title: Andrew Peacock, Shaddadids
sources.note: 2000, updated 2013. Distinguishes Ganja and Ani branches; critically discusses conflicting accounts of the 1075 transfer.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, Ganja
sources.note: 2000 scholarly city history. Earthquake dates vary in literary accounts; Gippert dates the earthquake and removal of the gate to 1139.

sources.title: Jost Gippert, The Gate of Ganja (2023)
sources.note: Caucasian Albania: An International Handbook, chapter 15A, printed pages 571 to 580. Gate translation page 573; AH 455 corresponds to 1063. Arabic original facsimile link was inaccessible; no reconstructed Arabic is published. Group with chapter 15 as one handbook for attribution.

sources.title: Igor Dorfmann-Lazarev, Between the Plains and the Mountains (2023)
sources.note: Author-uploaded full scholarly chapter 15, Caucasian Albania: An International Handbook, pages 537 to 570. Mixed families at Ganja discussed pages 558 to 559. Healing-baptism examples elsewhere concern southern Armenia, Asia Minor or Mardin and are not used as local medical evidence.

sources.title: Robert G. Hoyland, Fieldwork Report from Barda, Azerbaijan (2015)
sources.note: NYU Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, 30 November 2015. First season showed eleventh- to fourteenth-century settlement, challenging assumed abandonment.

sources.title: Barda Archaeological Expedition, Second Preliminary Field Report (2016)
sources.note: Oxford expedition report, printed pages 13 to 14, earliest medieval occupation dated by ceramics to eleventh through early thirteenth centuries. Later cesspits are not assigned to the 1000 to 1200 window.

sources.title: Barda Archaeological Expedition, Third Preliminary Field Report (2017)
sources.note: Printed pages 29 to 30, small finds from AEB01. Objects span medieval contexts; do not assign all finds to a single pre-1200 household. Report repeats one object number for different finds; catalogue numbers therefore omitted here.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, Baylaqan
sources.note: 1989 entry. Tenth-century geography is earlier background; Masud b. Namdar correspondence dates 1111 to 12. Mongol destruction date 1220 differs from 1221 in Arran entry; public prose uses early 1220s and retains return/rebuilding.

sources.title: Domenico Parrello, Khamsa of Nezami
sources.note: 2000, updated 2012. Five poems, manuscript transmission, sources and influence; Layli and Majnun completed 1188 with possible later additions.

sources.title: Zahra Taheri, Meter in Classical Persian Narrative Poetry (2012)
sources.note: In Hiroko Nagasaki, ed., Indian and Persian Prosody and Recitation, pages 45 to 58. Printed page 52, PDF page index 63, gives Nizami opening in Persian, metrical transcription and English translation. Original first hemistich also confirmed in indexed text and Ganjoor Layli and Majnun section 1; use only the poem, not Ganjoor AI glosses.

proposedOverrides.summary: A diverse medieval Caucasian region whose cities passed through Shaddadid, Seljuq and atabeg rule.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed record only, 1000 to 1200. Two near-identical polygons at the 1100 seam. No aliases. The Scotland/Isle of Arran lead is an identity mismatch and is rejected. Ancient Caucasian Albania and later names are not equivalent territorial or political entities.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two polygons bound approximately 46.4243 to 48.3719 E and 39.6654 to 40.9428 N. Barda and Baylaqan reference points lie inside; modern and approximate old Ganja points lie outside. Public overview explicitly states the imported outline cuts off the Ganja urban area. Dvin and Ani are outside and not treated as local Arran household sites.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No exact-window local medical institution, school curriculum or toilet system verified. Later Barda cesspits and late-antique/13th-century Qaratepe botanical material are not silently projected into 1000 to 1200. Gate Arabic facsimile inaccessible; genuine Persian sample used instead. David is a prescriptive critic, not a neutral household census. Manuscript dates distinguished from composition and modern printing.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Taheri’s printed Persian first hemistich and translation directly verified, with original text additionally checked against the indexed scholarly PDF and Ganjoor poem section 1. Romanization is a plain readable normalized rendering of the printed Persian, not a claim of medieval pronunciation. No original autograph claimed.
